newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga mulls bid for Kuwaiti KPC unit Santa Fe-report.
newsitem.headline: Saga mulls bid for Kuwaiti KPC unit Santa Fe-report.

text.p: Norway's largest independent oil company Saga Petroleum ASA is considering bidding for British-based Sante Fe Exploration, the business daily Dagens Naeringsliv (DN) said on Tuesday.
Santa Fe is valued at around $1 billion and Saga is expected to make an offer by November 1, DN said.
"Saga is evaluating the company at the moment, but they haven't made a formal offer yet," Michael Bourgeois, managing director in Sante Fe, was quoted as telling DN.
Saga spokesman Andreas Qvale could not confirm that the company was due to make a bid for Sante Fe.
"The economic situation of Saga is rather good. We are very interested in the British continental shelf and we are looking at opportunities all the time," Qvale told Reuters.
"But I cannot comment on whether or not we are in negotiations with Sante Fe."
Sante Fe Exploration is a subsidiary of KPC North Sea Holdings, which is wholly owned by state oil company Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC).
KPC announced on June 28 that it had decided to sell Sante Fe, whose North Sea holdings produced around 60,000 barrels per day in 1995.
